newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Public Bank to list subsidiaries.
newsitem.headline: Public Bank to list subsidiaries.

text.p: Public Bank Bhd said on Tuesday it is proposing a restructuring and listing of two of its subsidiaries through an investment holding company on the main board of the Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange.
The bank said in a statement that the restructuring and listing involves Public Consolidated Holdings Sdn Bhd, a 72-percent owned unit, and KL Mutual Fund Bhd, a 55-percent owned unit.
The listing would be done through investment holding company PBC Ventures Bhd.

Under the proposed restructuring, Public Consolidated would buy the remaining 30 percent it does not already own of PB Securities Sdn Bhd from Nizam Razak, a substantial shareholder of the securities firm. The consideration would be stock in Public Consolidated.
Public Consolidated would then conduct a rights issue of 29.57 million shares of 50 cents each.
PBC Ventures would then acquire 100 percent of Public Consolidated for a combination of new PBC stock and loan stocks, the statement said.
KL Mutual, a mutual funds firm, is proposing a rights issue of six million shares in a one-for-one ratio.
Following the rights scheme, which would boost the firm's share capital to 12 million ringgit from six million, PBC would acquire 100 percent of KL Mutual, the statement said.
After these two acquisitions, PBC would conduct a rights issue of 48.06 million new shares on a one-for-1.82 basis at a proposed issue price of 1.55 ringgit a piece.

Consequently, PBC proposes to make a public issue of 9.85 million new shares at a planned price of 7.60 ringgit a share. PBC will also hold a restricted issue of 4.4 million new shares at 7.60 ringgit to shareholders of Public Bank.
After the proposed listing of PBC, the firm will become a 54-percent owned unit of Public Bank. This percentage will be diluted to 50.43 percent after the full conversion of convertible loan stocks.
The proposals are subject to various regulatory approvals.
